transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-01 15:30 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rory Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO, Hummingbird), Samir Desai (Lead Platform Eng), Priya Rao (Dev Lead)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, can you all hear me?
[00:05] Lena Ortiz: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:08] Samir Desai: Good to go.
[00:12] Maya: Great. Quick agenda — walk through our self-serve API quickstart, how to get credits and TTFT, and then talk about your security / VPC questions. Rory will cover perf/cost.
[00:22] Rory Patel: Hi all. I'll start with a very short perf note: when you run the Redwood hosted API for chat with a 512 token prompt/response we typically see p95 latency in the 120–300ms per-token band depending on model and GPU; that maps to end-to-end ~400–800ms for a single 512 token generation on smaller models, and lower for trimmed contexts. Those numbers change on Dedicated — you get more predictable throughput and lower tail latencies.
[01:10] Priya Rao: Sorry to interrupt, when you say "per-token band" are we talking about our app's single-turn replies or streaming? Our UI streams tokens to the browser.
[01:18] Rory: Good question. Those numbers are for streaming output, continuous batching enabled. For TTFB (time-to-first-byte) we often hit 150–250ms for short outputs; full generation depends on token count.
[01:30] Lena: Our main ask is TTFT — we aim for a sub-second experience for short assistant replies, and we need predictability for peak hours. Also, data residency: some content must stay within EU.
[01:40] Maya: Totally. For TTFT the path is usually self-serve hosted to verify UX and developer integration — that's the fastest route to first token. We can enable trial credits so you can run real traffic patterns. For EU residency we have regional endpoints and can discuss Dedicated or Private if you need contractual residency guarantees.
[02:06] Samir: Can you outline what you mean by "trial credits" and how long they're live? Also, what data is retained by Redwood on hosted?
[02:12] Maya: We usually provide a credit bundle for PLG teams to get to first 30–90 days of testing — we'll do $5k of credits for your PoC, with clear expiration date in the activation email. On hosted, by default logs and traces are kept for telemetry; we have opt-out flags and redaction settings, and we offer enterprise retention controls for Dedicated/Private. I'll send the security pack with exact retention settings.
[02:45] Priya: Do you have SSO? Our engineers won't be happy building separate creds for each internal user.
[02:50] Maya: Yes, SSO via SAML/Okta or OIDC is supported. For Private/VPC we integrate with your IdP and you get RBAC and SCIM. We'll include the SSO integration guide.
[03:05] Rory: On the networking side — if you need VPC or on-prem, Redwood Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and we can package the runtime. That path involves more onboarding and procurement lead time — usually a few weeks to months depending on approvals. Dedicated is a middle ground: reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, and more isolation but still hosted by Redwood.
[03:35] Samir: Roughly how long to spin up Dedicated for a 2 GPU pool?
[03:39] Rory: If you sign a reserved capacity agreement we can provision within 2–4 weeks, depending on region and model choices. For an eval we can do a short Dedicated trial with burst capacity but that'll require a bit more paperwork.
[03:52] Lena: Okay. For a PLG initial test we want to self-serve, but we also need to know when it's time to go Dedicated or Private. What metrics or thresholds do you recommend?
[04:02] Rory: Common signals are predictable QPS above X rps where the cost curve tips in favor of Dedicated, tail latency spikes during peak, and compliance events (e.g., required contractual controls). We can build a run-book: tokens/day, P95 latency, and error budget thresholds. We'll share a simple spreadsheet mapping costs and break-even points.
[04:26] Priya: We also use KMS for key management. Does Redwood integrate with customer-managed keys?
[04:30] Maya: Yes — KMS integration is supported in Dedicated and Private. For hosted we offer envelope encryption and key rotation; enterprise customers can bring their keys for Private. We'll include the KMS/HSM options in the security doc.
[04:45] Samir: And audit logs — we need to produce logs for internal audits with per-request IDs. Can you get us the log formats?
[04:50] Rory: Audit logs with per-request metadata are available — we can stream logs to your S3 or to your SIEM in Dedicated/Private, and hosted can provide a subset via the console API. I'll attach a sample log payload.
[05:06] Maya: Quick demo idea — easiest way to prove TTFT is a quickstart where you post a request and stream responses. We have sample cURL, Node and Python snippets. Priya, do you want to run one live?
[05:18] Priya: Yes, we can try after this call. We'll need the keys and credentials though.
[05:22] Maya: I'll enable the trial credit pack and send activation steps. You can then hit the hosted endpoint from your staging environment and measure TTFT.
[05:30] Lena: What about obfuscation/redaction? Some of our prompts include PII.
[05:35] Rory: We have server-side redaction hooks and prefix/KV caching controls. For PII, we recommend client-side redaction plus server-side redaction rules for sensitive fields during eval. We'll send examples.
[05:48] Samir: Cost question — if we spin up a small Dedicated pool vs staying on hosted and running 100k tokens/day, what's the ballpark difference?
[05:56] Rory: Quick ballpark — hosted variable costs might be $X per 1k tokens depending on model; Dedicated reduces per-token cost substantially when you have steady throughput because the infra is reserved. I'll run a 30/60/90 day projection and show the break-even GT (tokens/day).
[06:18] Priya: Are there any limits on streaming/webhook connections? We have thousands of concurrent browsers, but each session doesn't stream huge.
[06:26] Maya: Hosted supports many concurrent connections with autoscaling but Dedicated gives you reserved concurrency. We'll note your session pattern and recommend a config.
[06:38] Lena: Timeline-wise, we want to ship an internal prototype in three weeks. Can the quickstart get us there?
[06:45] Maya: Absolutely — that's the exact use case. We aim for TTFT as soon as you have an API key and a small integration (front-end token streaming). Usually teams get their first tokens in under an hour, and a production-like prototype in days.
[06:58] Samir: One more compliance: do you offer SOC 2 Type II?
[07:03] Maya: Yes, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II. That packet and our ISO documentation will be in the pack I send.
[07:10] [short pause, typing noises]
[07:20] Priya: Cool. From engineering side, our devs will want to test with the exact model flavor — can we pick a specific open model you host?
[07:27] Rory: Yes, our catalog includes curated models and model variants; for the trial we can point you at a cost-performance balanced choice. If you need quantized variants for lower latency/cost tradeoffs we can recommend one.
[07:40] Lena: Will you share benchmarks for a 512 token chat and a 2048 token doc summarize?
[07:45] Rory: Yes — I'll attach a short benchmark table and a small runbook showing which kernels/quantization were used. The benchmark will be sample-based and will include p50/p95/token latency and cost per 1k tokens.
[07:58] Maya: Ok, let's recap the concrete next steps so everyone is aligned: 1) Maya activates $5k trial credits and sends quickstart snippets + activation link; 2) Rory sends cost/latency projection and sample logs + benchmark table; 3) Redwood shares SOC2, SSO and VPC/KMS integration docs; 4) Hummingbird to confirm security contact and pick a slot for a hands-on session. Anything to add?
[08:26] Samir: Could you also include the Dedicated provisioning lead time and an outline of contract terms? We won't sign immediately but want to know the cadence.
[08:33] Maya: Sure, I'll include a short dedicated provisioning FAQ and the typical contract timelines.
[08:37] Priya: We'll follow up with a sample request body for the 512 token case — I can send that to Rory.
[08:43] Maya: Great. We'll send calendar options for next-week quickstart.
[08:47] Lena: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[08:50] Maya: Thank you, talk soon.

End of transcript.
